terms.name: Accessibility trait
terms.definition: The platform flag on a native view that says what it is and how it behaves, the mobile counterpart to a role plus a state, and the thing a custom control has to set by hand.

terms.name: Alert dialog
terms.definition: A dialog that interrupts the flow to demand acknowledgement or confirmation of a consequential action before anything else can continue.

terms.name: ARIA notify
terms.definition: A proposed API for speaking a message directly to assistive technology, without the live region trick of mutating hidden text and hoping the timing works out.

terms.name: Axis
terms.definition: The ruled edge of a chart that maps position to value: scale, ticks, and labels that make the marks readable as numbers.

terms.name: Brand color
terms.definition: The colour an organisation owns in a customer's memory, carried into a product as the seed for its palette rather than used directly on every surface.

terms.name: Cap height
terms.definition: The height of a capital letter measured from the baseline, and the edge designers usually mean when they say text should line up flush.

terms.name: Chart description
terms.definition: The text alternative for a chart: a summary of the takeaway plus access to the underlying values, not a recital of the pixels.

terms.name: Code editor
terms.definition: A text area specialised for code, with a gutter of line numbers, syntax colouring and a caret that understands indentation.

terms.name: Color token
terms.definition: A named colour decision stored once and referenced everywhere, so retheming is a change to the value rather than an edit at every place it is used.

terms.name: Confetti burst
terms.definition: A short particle celebration thrown across the screen to mark a completion, decorative by design and the first thing reduced motion should drop.

terms.name: Contribution graph
terms.definition: A year of days as a grid of week columns, each cell shaded by how much happened that day, so a habit reads as a pattern instead of a number.

terms.name: Dark mode
terms.definition: A second palette built on dark surfaces with light foregrounds, derived from the light one by rebalancing lightness and saturation rather than by inverting it.

terms.name: Descender
terms.definition: The part of a letter such as g, j, p, or y that drops below the baseline.

terms.name: Diverging palette
terms.definition: A data palette built from two sequential scales meeting at a neutral midpoint, used when values run above and below a meaningful zero.

terms.name: Drip pricing
terms.definition: Advertising a low headline price and adding mandatory fees one screen at a time, so the true total only appears once the buyer is committed.

terms.name: Elevation overlay
terms.definition: The older dark theme technique of laying white over a surface at an opacity that rises with elevation, because shadows are nearly invisible on dark backgrounds.

terms.name: Expanded state
terms.definition: The open or closed state of a disclosure, exposed with aria-expanded on the control that owns it rather than on the panel it reveals.

terms.name: Feed layout
terms.definition: A scrolling column or adaptive grid of equivalent items built for browsing, where no item outranks another by position alone.

terms.name: Flat design
terms.definition: A style that strips away depth cues, using solid fills, sharp edges, and bold color instead of shadow, gradient, bevel, or texture.

terms.name: Focus ring
terms.definition: The visible outline drawn around the element that currently holds keyboard focus, showing where the next keypress will land.

terms.name: FOUT
terms.definition: The visible swap when a page first paints text in a fallback face and then re-renders it once the web font arrives.

terms.name: Goal gradient
terms.definition: Effort rising as a visible goal gets closer, which is why interfaces show how little is left rather than how much has been done.

terms.name: Hand-drawn UI
terms.definition: A style whose lines wobble as if sketched by hand, used to signal that a diagram or wireframe is provisional rather than finished.

terms.name: Hold to confirm
terms.definition: Requiring a press to be held for a moment before a destructive action commits, with progress shown so the wait is understood as deliberate.

terms.name: Icon button
terms.definition: A button whose whole label is an icon, so it needs an accessible name and usually a tooltip to say what it does.

terms.name: Input mask
terms.definition: A field that imposes a fixed shape as you type, inserting the slashes, spaces or brackets a phone number or card number needs.

terms.name: Juiciness
terms.definition: Stacking far more feedback on an act than it needs, so one small input wobbles, pops and sings, and the interface feels alive under the hand.

terms.name: Label in name
terms.definition: The rule that a control's accessible name must contain its visible label text, so speaking the visible words works in voice control.

terms.name: Letterpress text
terms.definition: A text effect that fakes stamping into the surface, using a one pixel light shadow below the glyphs and a slightly darker fill above it.

terms.name: Live region
terms.definition: A container marked so assistive technology reads changes inside it without moving focus, used for messages that appear after an action.

terms.name: Marquee
terms.definition: Text or logos that scroll continuously across a strip, either as a decorative ticker or because a label is too long for its box.

terms.name: Mica
terms.definition: Fluent's opaque app background material, subtly tinted with the user's desktop wallpaper colour and going neutral when the window loses focus.

terms.name: Modular scale
terms.definition: A type scale generated by multiplying a base size by a fixed ratio, so every step is proportionally related to the one before it.

terms.name: Name, role, value
terms.definition: The three things every control has to expose to assistive technology: what it is called, what kind of thing it is, and what state it is currently in.

terms.name: Non-text contrast
terms.definition: The requirement that controls, focus indicators and meaningful graphics reach 3:1 against what is next to them, which is the rule that governs borders and icons.

terms.name: Optical alignment
terms.definition: Nudging an element off its measured position so it looks aligned, correcting for shapes whose bounding box lies about their visual centre.

terms.name: Overview plus detail
terms.definition: A layout that shows a compressed overview and a detailed view at the same time in separate regions, so the reader keeps their place while inspecting one part.

terms.name: Pause, stop, hide
terms.definition: A visible control for content that moves, blinks, scrolls, or updates on its own, so a reader can stop it before reading around it.

terms.name: Pointer lock
terms.definition: Hiding the cursor and reading only its movement deltas, so input keeps flowing past the edges of the screen instead of stopping at them.

terms.name: Primitive color token
terms.definition: A raw palette value named for what it is, like blue-500, sitting under the semantic layer that names colours for what they do.

terms.name: Pulse
terms.definition: A slow repeating change in scale or opacity that keeps an element alive without moving it, used for waiting states and gentle attention.

terms.name: Read aloud
terms.definition: Speaking a page's own prose with a synthetic voice, highlighting each word as it is spoken. A reading aid for people who can see the screen, not a screen reader.

terms.name: Responsive upscaling
terms.definition: Designing what a layout does with the space it gains on very wide screens, rather than only what it drops as screens narrow.

terms.name: RTL mirroring
terms.definition: Flipping a layout horizontally for right to left languages, moving navigation and progression to the other side while leaving some elements unmirrored.

terms.name: Scroll chaining
terms.definition: When an inner scroller reaches its end and the gesture continues, the scroll passes to the page behind it unless that handoff is blocked.

terms.name: Segmented control
terms.definition: A single control holding two to five mutually exclusive options side by side, with the current one shown as a filled segment.

terms.name: Share sheet
terms.definition: The system panel of destinations and actions for sending the current item elsewhere, populated by whatever apps are installed.

terms.name: Sliding indicator
terms.definition: A single underline or pill that travels between tabs to mark the selection instead of each tab drawing its own, so the move itself says which way the selection went.

terms.name: Spacing scale
terms.definition: The fixed, named set of spacing values a system allows, so gaps come from a shortlist instead of being invented per screen.

terms.name: Squircle
terms.definition: A rounded square whose corners curve continuously into the sides instead of meeting a circular arc, the shape behind iOS app icons.

terms.name: Sticky header
terms.definition: A header that scrolls away with the page until it reaches the top edge, then stays fixed there while the rest keeps moving.

terms.name: Swash
terms.definition: A letter drawn with an ornamental flourish, usually an extended entry or exit stroke on an italic capital.

terms.name: Tabs
terms.definition: A set of labelled panels in one region, where selecting a label swaps the panel beneath it.

terms.name: Thumb zone
terms.definition: The arc of a phone screen a thumb reaches comfortably in a one handed grip, with harder to reach bands above and across from it.

terms.name: Tooltip
terms.definition: A brief text label shown on hover or keyboard focus that names or explains the element it points at, and carries nothing you can interact with.

terms.name: Truncation
terms.definition: Cutting text that does not fit and marking the cut, usually with an ellipsis, so the reader knows something was removed.

terms.name: Utility navigation
terms.definition: The strip of secondary tools and account actions, sign in, search, language, cart, kept apart from the links that describe the site's content.

terms.name: Visually hidden
terms.definition: Content removed from the visual layout but left in the accessibility tree, so screen readers announce what the design leaves unsaid.

terms.name: X-height
terms.definition: The height of a lowercase x in a typeface, measured from the baseline, which is what makes two fonts at the same point size look different sizes.
